documents.title: What the Co-Pilot can do: tasks, contacts, appointments, the calendar, searching, dates, roles and limits
documents.content: The Co-Pilot is the AI assistant in the side panel and on its own page. You must be signed in to use it: who you are, which workspace you are in and your role come from your sign-in, never from what the browser sends. It can search Ogeemo pages and the contacts and projects of your own workspace (by name, company, email or a phone number typed any way), create a task, a to-do or a calendar event, create a project, add a contact, add up your hours and unbilled time, read your invoices and quotes, and explain how Ogeemo works (it looks the detail up in this Knowledge Base). It cannot list time entries, read payroll, the ledger or the bank, and it cannot edit or delete tasks, projects, invoices or quotes. Creating a task needs the editor, org_admin or super_admin role; a viewer can ask questions but is told an editor must create the task. A task it creates appears in the Activity Manager and, when it has no date and no project, on the To-Do List; a task for a project also becomes a step of that project. The contact and project must belong to your workspace. The Co-Pilot is told today's date and your time zone, so "tomorrow at 3pm" or "next Friday" is worked out from your own clock; a time with no offset is read in your zone, an end time defaults to one hour after the start, and an end before the start is refused. If the Co-Pilot is unsure of the time it asks. It only says a task was created when it was really saved; otherwise it gives the reason. The search never invents people: earlier versions listed made-up "Dan" and "Julie" contacts for any search containing those letters. "Sync receipts" tells you plainly that Google Drive is not connected yet and points to Receipt Intake, instead of listing made-up PDFs. To protect the service, each person can send about 30 Co-Pilot or Knowledge Base messages a minute, 20 sandbox questions and 6 images; past that a message asks you to wait a few seconds. A message can be at most 4,000 characters (2,000 in the Knowledge Base) and only the recent conversation is sent.

documents.title: Co-Pilot: adding a contact
documents.content: Ask it to add a contact (for example "add Jane Doe, jane@acme.com, in Clients") and it saves the contact straight away, in your workspace, in the way the Contacts Hub does: only the name is needed, the folder is optional and the workspace default folder is used when none is named, and the email must look like an email address. Adding a contact needs the editor, org_admin or super_admin role. Before adding, it checks for a contact with the same email address or the same name; if it finds one it adds nothing, tells you who matched and asks whether to add another anyway. It does not add Employees or Contractors (those need pay and Document Manager setup, so use the Workers page at /workers) and it never takes a SIN, pay rate or employment dates. It only says a contact was added when it was really saved.

documents.title: Co-Pilot: booking, moving and cancelling appointments, and reading your calendar
documents.content: Ask it to book an appointment (for example "book a meeting with Dana tomorrow at 3pm for 30 minutes") and it saves an appointment on your Calendar, in your workspace and under your name: it needs a day and a time of day (it asks if either is missing), the length is an hour unless you say otherwise, a time that has already passed is refused, and a contact, if you name one, must be in your workspace. Booking needs the editor, org_admin or super_admin role. Before booking, it checks your own calendar: if the time overlaps one of your unfinished events it books nothing, tells you which event it overlaps and suggests the next free time (9:00 to 17:00 in your time zone, weekdays), and books over it only if you say to. Other people's calendars are never checked or shown. Ask "what is on tomorrow?" or "am I free at 3?" and it reads your own calendar and answers from it. Ask it to move or cancel an event ("move my 3pm to 4pm", "cancel my 2pm") and it shows what it would do, says nothing has changed yet, and only acts when you answer with a plain yes; a yes that adds anything starts over. It changes only your own events, only their time or a cancel, and refuses to cancel one that is on an invoice, has recorded time or an open work order. It cannot delete a task, project or invoice. It only says an appointment is booked, moved or cancelled when it really happened.

documents.title: Co-Pilot: making a to-do and adding a project
documents.content: Ask it to make a to-do (for example "make a to-do: call the bank" or "remind me to call Dana on Friday at 2") and it saves it as a task: only a title is needed, a to-do with no date and no project goes on the To-Do List, and one with a day and time also appears on the Calendar. Ask it to add a project (for example "add a new project called Website Redesign") and it saves the project in your workspace with Planning status, the way the New Project screen does: only the name is needed, a description and a client contact are optional, and the steps are planned afterwards in the Project Planner. It checks for a project with the same name (case and spacing ignored); if one exists it creates nothing, tells you, and creates another only if you say to. Creating a project needs the editor, org_admin or super_admin role, and it only says a project was created when it was really saved.

documents.title: Co-Pilot: hours worked and unbilled time
documents.content: Ask "how many hours did I work this week?", "what is unbilled?" or "how much can I bill Dana?" and it adds up your time from the same records and with the same billing rules as the Time Log Report: worked hours, billable hours, unbilled hours and their value (worked, billable, with a client, not yet on an invoice), hours already invoiced, and unbilled hours per client. Billable time with no client is reported separately because it cannot be invoiced yet, and time that is only scheduled and not yet worked is reported separately and never counted. You see your own time; an org_admin or super_admin can ask for the whole workspace. It gives totals only, not individual entries: open the Time Log Report at /reports/time-log for the rows.

documents.title: Co-Pilot: who owes you money, overdue invoices and open quotes
documents.content: Ask "who owes me money?", "what is overdue?", "has Dana paid?" or "what is the status of INV-1042?" and it reads your invoices the way Accounts Receivable does: balance owed is the total less payments to the cent, an invoice is overdue from the day after its due date while money is still owed (counted in your own time zone), a part-paid invoice can be overdue, and drafts are left out unless you ask for them. Ask "what quotes are open?" or "which quotes need follow-up?" and it reads your quotes the way the Quote Manager does: a quote needs attention when it has been Sent for 14 days or more with no change, is Approved but not yet invoiced or turned into a work order, or is still Requested, Draft or Sent and expires within 7 days. It shows the number, client, dates, amounts and status of up to 15 records plus totals, and never notes, addresses, business numbers or line items. Reading invoices and quotes needs the editor, org_admin or super_admin role (a viewer is told an editor must ask) and a menu that shows Accounts Receivable or the Quote Manager. It cannot post a payment or send, approve, convert or change an invoice or quote; use Accounts Receivable or the Quote Manager for that.

documents.title: Image Generator: how it works, limits and why an image may fail
documents.content: The Image Generator at /tools/image-generator turns a short description into a picture using Google's Gemini image model. You must be signed in. Describe what you want in up to 1,000 characters, choose Generate, and download the result when it appears. Each image is billed to Ogeemo, so you can make about 6 a minute; past that a message tells you how many seconds to wait. If the image service is busy you are asked to try again in a minute, and if it returns no picture you are asked to describe the image differently. Technical error details are written to the server log and are not shown on screen. The generator used to ask for a model (imagen-3) that Google no longer offers for this account, so every request failed; it now uses gemini-2.5-flash-image.
